classify.title: AI category auto-classification
classify.sub: Paste the text you want to post and we'll show candidate sections, categories and grades along with the words behind them.
classify.eng: Rule engine. Server-side industry vocabulary (classify_vocab) · restricted industries · banned-word list.
classify.how: Each word has a weight; we add up the weights of words found in the text per category and convert them to ratios. Amounts · regions · specs are extracted with regular expressions. Restricted industries are blocked before scoring.
classify.lim: It is not a trained model. If a word isn't in the vocabulary, it says it couldn't classify. It doesn't understand context, irony or typos, and when the same word is used in several industries it's decided by weights alone. Per-word weights are not shown (to prevent gaming the rules).
classify.next: The industries users actually choose ("Post in this section") are logged. If choices keep differing from suggestions, we adjust the word weights. When a real model is added, this log becomes training and evaluation data.

match.title: AI recommendations
match.sub: Ranks business candidates for one request by a weighted score across 5 factors. Move the weights and the ranking is recalculated instantly.
match.loadFail: Couldn't load recommendations. Please try again shortly.
match.noRequest: You haven't posted a request yet. Recommendations rank candidates for one of your referral requests.
match.oneToOne: This request goes to one business only. We never sell the same request to multiple businesses (no resale), so the ranking is the allocation.
match.eng: Rule engine. Weighted average of 5 factors — region · category · deal history · response speed · trust (server fn_request_candidates).
match.how: Each candidate gets factor scores (0–100) from real data — region (business address · city · district) · category (listings in the same industry) · confirmed deals × 20 · average first-reply time (0 at 72+ hours) · verification 40 + review stars. The on-screen weights produce the weighted average. Missing verification doesn't reduce the score; it is shown on the card as is.
match.lim: It is not collaborative filtering. Until deal data builds up, these weights are the basis of the recommendation, and whoever sets them is the algorithm. Factors without records score 0.
match.next: Once deal logs build up, weights will be learned from close rates. The hook is the server function that builds factor scores (fn_request_candidates).

matchView.sum: Total {n} — it doesn't need to add up to 100. Ratios are used.
matchView.adWhy: This is a sponsored slot. It is not included in scoring and doesn't appear in the ranking — mixing ads with recommendations would violate the Fair Labeling and Advertising Act.
matchView.empty: No business listings are live in this request's section yet — candidates will be ranked here once there are some.
matchView.noBiz: No business verification — if the deal closes, the referral fee is paid to an individual (identity verification · payout account check).
matchView.okBiz: Verification OK — a referral code is issued when you start a 1:1 inquiry.

profile.title: Interest profile
profile.sub: Six questions sort your interests. The result is used for home ads and recommendation sorting.
profile.noteFallback: We add up your choices and use the highest segment. No inference.
profile.loadFail: Couldn't load the questions. Please try again shortly.
profile.eng: Rule engine. {n} questions · per-option segment weight table (server) · 6 segments.
profile.how: The weights of your chosen options are added per segment and the highest is used. Ties go to the earlier segment.
profile.lim: Behavior data is not used. Only your own answers count, so it may differ from your real interests, and it changes as soon as you change your answers. Six questions don't define a person.
profile.next: Adding browsing · search · deal history would produce segments without questions. Before that, the collected items and retention period must be added to the privacy policy.
